title: Dragonwings (Selected Chapters & The Dream of Flight)
author: Laurence Yep

sections.heading: Moon Shadow's Arrival in the Land of the Golden Mountain

epigraph.quote: Whenever we Tang men looked west, we thought of the Land of the Golden Mountain. But when I arrived in San Francisco, the demon buildings were cold and gray.

paragraphs: In 1903, eight-year-old Moon Shadow leaves his mother and grandmother in their rural village in southern China to sail across the Pacific to San Francisco, joining the father he has never seen. Like thousands of Chinese immigrants (the 'Tang people'), Moon Shadow's father, Windrider, works grueling hours in a Chinatown laundry, enduring racial hostility and anti-Chinese immigration laws.

To Moon Shadow, America is the 'Land of the Golden Mountain,' but the reality is harsh: Chinatown is a crowded enclave bordered by hostile white 'demons.' Yet Moon Shadow discovers that his father is no ordinary laundryman. Windrider is a mechanical genius, an artist, and a dreamer who believes that in a previous life he was a majestic dragon physician in the heavenly court of the Dragon King.

sections.heading: The 1906 Earthquake and The Flight of the Aeroplane

epigraph.quote: If men can fly, Moon Shadow, then dragons can truly soar again.

paragraphs: Inspired by reports of the Wright brothers' historic flight at Kitty Hawk in 1903, Windrider dedicates every penny of his savings and every late-night hour to designing and constructing a full-scale flying machine he names 'Dragonwings.' When the catastrophic 1906 San Francisco earthquake and subsequent fires raze Chinatown to ash, Windrider and Moon Shadow relocate to the Oakland hills, sheltered by a kind white woman, Miss Whitlaw, and her niece.

In the novel's breathtaking climax, Windrider, Moon Shadow, and their loyal Chinatown companions haul the bamboo-and-silk aeroplane to the crest of the windy Berkeley hills. Igniting the engine, Windrider hurtles down the grassy slope and lifts into the sky, soaring for three glorious minutes over the bay before crash-landing safely. In that brief, magnificent flight, Windrider and Moon Shadow prove that courage and imagination can shatter racial prejudice and transcend human limits.
